citations.S1: builds the query by string interpolation with values that come straight from the HTTP request. Fix: use parameterized queries
citations.S2: `conn`/`cur` are never closed, and there's no `try`/`finally` or context manager, so on any exception ... the connection leaks
citations.S3: `order[0]` is the numeric order ID from SQLite (an int); `"Order #" + order[0]` raises `TypeError: can only concatenate str`
citations.S5: Money stored/handled as `float` — high (data integrity)... Fix: use `Decimal` (ideally the DB itself should store integer minor units/cents)
citations.S6: A negative `pct` increases the price; `pct > 100` produces a negative amount. Fix: clamp/reject outside `[0, 100]`
citations.S7: `status` should be validated against a known set of order statuses at the boundary
citations.S8: `user_id` comes from the request, and this function trusts it with no check that it matches the authenticated caller
citations.S10: `apply_discount` and `format_receipt` don't round, so results can show as `19.999999999997`
citations.S11: Any `sqlite3.Error` propagates unhandled up to the HTTP layer, risking a raw DB error (schema/path detail) reaching the client
citations.S12: Round once, at the point of display/storage, with a stated policy (half-up here)
citations.S13: No `LIMIT`/pagination; a user with an enormous order history returns everything in one query
